description:
We are students at FEUP (MEGI+MESG). Our strengths are decision support, optimization, operations management and data analysis.

If you like turning data into real-world decisions, join us!
summary:
We built a decision-support tool that helps farmers compare crop rotations for soil health and climate resilience, piloted in Bragança, north-east Portugal. There, the current rotation (potato, wheat, fallow) leaves soil bare for about 250 days a year, exposing it to erosion, drought and heavy rain.
The tool compares this rotation with three alternatives: a legume or a forage crop instead of fallow, and a hardy cereal followed by a legume. Using 25 years of NASA POWER climate data, it estimates bare-soil days, erosion risk, water deficit and frost exposure for each one. A 0–100 score weights these by the farmer’s own priorities, set with sliders in a Streamlit app. Particle swarm optimisation shows how much those priorities would need to change to alter the top choice, and Sentinel-2 NDVI checks bare-soil periods on local fields.
With equal priorities, the hardy-cereal rotation ranks first in every scenario, and replacing fallow cuts bare-soil days to 158–184. Each strategy comes with its rationale, uncertainty and risks, and the assumptions were reviewed by a local agronomist. Because NASA POWER is global, the approach can be reused on other farms. The tool supports the farmer’s judgement rather than replacing it.
details:
What it does
Field Shift is a web app that compares crop rotations for soil health and climate resilience. Our pilot farm in Bragança, Portugal, rotates potato, wheat and fallow. We compare it with three alternatives: a legume or forage crop instead of fallow, or a hardy cereal followed by a legume.

How it works
Using 26 years of NASA POWER data, the app estimates each rotation’s bare-soil days, erosion risk, water deficit and frost exposure. It then gives each one a 0–100 score weighted by the farmer’s priorities. Sentinel-2 NDVI checks when local fields are really bare.

Benefits and impact
Farmers set their own priorities and constraints and see results for dry, heavy-rain and all years, with the evidence, unknowns and risks of each option. Replacing the fallow cuts bare-soil days from about 250 to 158–184 a year, which means less erosion and more organic matter.

Tools
Python (Streamlit, NumPy, Folium), NASA POWER and ESA Sentinel-2. Code written with Claude as a coding assistant, directed and reviewed by the team. Code: github.com/salvadorbrosa/CSM-Nablus2026

Creativity
We use particle swarm optimisation to test how robust the ranking is, not to pick it. Moving 8% of the weight from water to organic matter changes the top rotation.

Factors considered
The tool is simple to use and was reviewed by a local agronomist. It is also honest about its limits: the climate data is regional and prices are estimates. It supports the farmer’s decision but does not replace it.
